title: Nucleus: Cost Threads dashboard - token-level decomposition & export probe
creator: Maya Alvarez
description: Design and prototype a new Console panel called 'Nucleus: Cost Threads' that surfaces token-level cost breakdowns and multi-dimensional attribution for sessions, prompts, and model variants. The goal is to let engineers and finance teams quickly unravel why a given bill line exists, export granular slices for downstream analysis, and provide role-aware pricing pattern recommendations (batching suggestions, quantization flags, and slab/volume pricing insights). This ticket covers interaction patterns, two visual density variants, CSV/Parquet export, and lightweight previewing for very large result sets.
acceptance_criteria: Primary panel mockups exist for Compact and Expanded density with documented interactions
User can filter by time range, model, route, session id, and prompt tag in the prototype
Export flow supports CSV and Parquet, with permission gating and size warning modal
Attribution waterfall view shows token origin (system/prompt/completion/assistant) and cost per-token breakdown
Pricing pattern hints panel surfaces 3 automated suggestions and links to Optimize settings
Design handoff includes annotated Figma screens, accessibility notes, and interaction specs for engineering
decisions: Use server-side pre-aggregation for per-session token summaries to avoid streaming full token logs into the client
Default view should be Compact (collapsed rows) with on-demand expansion to preserve vertical real estate for power users
Export will be generated asynchronously and delivered via S3 link with scoped download permissions to avoid browser memory limits
tradeoffs: Inline expansion vs modal detail: inline keeps context but can be heavy for many rows; chosen approach favors inline with progressive disclosure and a 'Full Record' modal for heavy inspection
Pre-aggregation accuracy vs freshness: to meet latency SLOs we will show near-real-time aggregates (1-2 minute refresh) and surface a freshness timestamp
Rich client-side filtering vs server queries: complex multi-facet filters will be server-backed to avoid shipping large result sets
implementation_notes: Frontend: Virtualized table (react-window) + column virtualization for token columns
Backend: New /cost/threads/aggregate endpoint (ENG-22134) returns per-session and per-prompt slices with normalized token counts
Export: Job queued (celery/k8s job) with signed S3 URL returned to UI (link valid 72h)
Telemetry: Instrument filter usage, expansion events, export requests; add perf markers to measure typical expand latency
review_comments: PM (Amira Shah): Please ensure pricing-hints copy is actionable for non-ML finance folks — include example savings in dollars and percent
Eng (Luca Romano): Concern about constructing per-token attribution for very long conversations — recommend capped preview and 'request full export' CTA
Security (Ravi Patel): Exports contain session ids and potentially PII in prompts — enforce role-based gating and audit logs
Design (Maya Alvarez): Updated expanded row to use color-coded token bands (system/prompt/assistant) after usability testing
usability_findings: 5 users (2 SRE, 2 FinOps, 1 PM) tested compact vs expanded: all preferred compact for day-to-day + expanded for incident triage
Users found the waterfal l visualization valuable but wanted clearer labeling of cost units (USD per 1k tokens) — added tooltip
Export flow needs explicit size estimation and 'approximate time to deliver' to set expectations
related_prs: GH-9921: export job worker and signed-url flow
GH-10013: server aggregation endpoint and query optimizer

Finalize copy for pricing-hints with PM and Finance (Amira Shah)
Run a security review for export scope and gating; file follow-up if needed
Handoff to ENG with Figma spec + acceptance criteria; schedule 2-week check-in
